clue.text: Servant who told of Ernest Pontifex

definitions.meaning: a household's chief manservant, in charge of the wine and the table
Samuel ... novel The Way of All Flesh tells the life of Ernest Pontifex

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a servant, and the surname of Samuel Butler, author of The Way of All Flesh, whose hero is Ernest Pontifex.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a domestic job title; the second is the surname of the Victorian novelist who wrote Ernest's story.

clue.text: Ancient city detailed by very English chart-topper

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, having its tail cut off

parts.note: Babylon was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An old city depicted by a thoroughly English best-selling record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'described minutely'; it means the city loses its last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supremes' 1964 hit Baby Love reached number one in both the US and UK charts.

clue.text: Incomplete notion about an old king being Der Hofmeister

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round another piece
incomplete means the notion word is missing its last letter

parts.note: a theory is a notion or idea
Tut, the Egyptian boy king Tutankhamun

explanation.surface: A half-formed idea about an ancient monarch who was a German court official.
explanation.walkthrough: Lenz's play Der Hofmeister (1774) is known in English under this title; 'Incomplete' drops the notion's last letter and 'about' sets it round the boy king.
explanation.definitionFit: Der Hofmeister is J M R Lenz's 1774 German play, known in English by this title.

clue.text: Quote brought up to encapsulate hard moral value

indicators.note: to encapsulate means the turned word encloses another piece
brought up means the quote word is turned upwards, read bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: to quote is to cite
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A citation is raised to sum up a stern principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns CITE into ETIC; 'to encapsulate' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or set of values guiding conduct.

clue.text: Coastal town captain, pal to a sleuth

definitions.meaning: a resort on the East Sussex coast of England, site of the 1066 battle
Agatha Christie's Captain Arthur, friend and chronicler of Hercule Poirot

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: an English seaside town in East Sussex, and the surname of Captain Arthur, Poirot's companion in Agatha Christie's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a Sussex seaside resort and to Poirot's loyal military friend and narrator.

clue.text: Emerges outside leading hotel with an old playwright

indicators.note: outside means the first word sits round the others

parts.note: arises means comes up, emerges
top means leading, first
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet
the word itself

explanation.surface: Someone surfaces outside the best hotel with a veteran dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' looks like a participle with the hotel; it means TOP. 'outside' sets the emerging word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes was the comic dramatist of ancient Athens, author of The Frogs and Lysistrata.

clue.text: State a dramatist's first name

definitions.meaning: a southern US state, capital Nashville
... Williams, author of A Streetcar Named Desire

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: a US state, and the forename of the playwright Tennessee Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright Thomas Lanier Williams took his chosen forename from the American state.

clue.text: Biblical scholars Eberhard and Erwin get comfy

definitions.meaning: father and son who edited the standard Greek New Testament text
to settle snugly into a comfortable position

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: the surname of Eberhard and Erwin, editors of the Greek New Testament (later Nestle-Aland), and to snuggle down.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a German scholarly surname; the other is the verb meaning to settle cosily.

clue.text: Jael stuck him in a temple

definitions.text: Jael stuck him in a temple

parts.words: Jael stuck him in a temple
parts.note: in Judges 4 Jael kills the fleeing Canaanite general by driving a tent peg through his head; temple is the side of the head, not a shrine

explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' suggests a place of worship; it is the side of the head, where Jael drove the tent peg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names the Canaanite commander whom Jael killed with a tent peg as he slept.

clue.text: Book about gossip left by a dramatist

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: left by means the following letter has departed, dropped out of the word before it

parts.note: to gossip is to chat
the letter itself

explanation.surface: A volume about tittle-tattle that a playwright left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by a' reads as abandoned by a dramatist, but it means the gossip word loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was the German playwright of Mother Courage and The Threepenny Opera.

clue.text: Backtracking church council accepts one American God

indicators.note: accepts means the turned word takes in another piece within it
backtracking means the word for the council runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a synod is an assembly of church clergy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A church assembly goes back on itself and admits a single American deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backtracking' turns the council round (DONYS) before 'accepts' takes in the one; 'God' with a capital looks monotheistic but is a Greek deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dionysus was the Greek god of wine and revelry.

clue.text: Outstanding carvings a looter's evil destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the words are wrecked and reassembled in another order

parts.note: looter's supplies all its letters including the S

explanation.surface: Fine sculptures wrecked by the wickedness of a plunderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is the definition's pun: the carvings stand out from their background.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto-relievo is high relief, sculpture projecting strongly from its ground, so it literally stands out.

clue.text: Good deal on fabric cut by a Parisian knight

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it
cut by means the fabric word is split open with another piece set inside

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a lot means a good deal, a large amount

explanation.surface: A bargain on cloth trimmed by a French gentleman of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' sets the French article inside the fabric, giving LAUNCE; 'on' puts it ahead of the good deal in this across clue. Launcelot is an old spelling of Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Launcelot (Lancelot) is the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: European king needing his first mathematician

indicators.note: needing his first means the king word lacks its opening letter

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A continental monarch who requires his first-born, or perhaps a numbers expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing his first' reads as wanting his heir; it means the king word lacks its first letter. The answer is pronounced 'oiler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician of enormous output.

clue.text: Flower ceremony with organ primarily as backing instrument

parts.note: the viola is a garden flower related to the pansy
pomp is stately ceremony and display

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of organ is taken
as backing means the little word as runs from right to left

explanation.surface: Flowers, a ceremony and an organ playing accompaniment at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives O from organ; 'as backing' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola pomposa is an eighteenth-century stringed instrument, a large five-string viola.

clue.text: A bold male next to which Paris's no hero

parts.note: game means bold, plucky, willing
non is the French for no, as said in Paris

explanation.surface: A brave man beside whom Paris of Troy looks no hero at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the Trojan prince; it is the French city, giving NON.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, led the Greeks at Troy, a hero of the Iliad.

clue.text: Sinister mentor initially seems good in an evil novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a fresh arrangement
initially means the first letters of seems and good are taken

explanation.surface: A menacing tutor seems benign at first in a wicked book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S and G, set with AN EVIL and rearranged; 'novel' looks like a book but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's Trilby, now any sinister controlling mentor.

clue.text: Lloyd, Stevenson's collaborator in rating Ludlum's supremacy

parts.note: OS, ordinary seaman, is a naval rating
Robert Ludlum wrote The Bourne Supremacy, so his supremacy is Bourne's

explanation.surface: A writer's partner takes part in judging a thriller's standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like assessing; it is a sailor, OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd Osbourne, Robert Louis Stevenson's stepson, co-wrote The Wrong Box and The Ebb-Tide with him.

clue.text: The body in the library tales by Richardson and Chaucer

parts.note: Samuel Richardson's novel Pamela, or Virtue Rewarded
The Reeve's Tale is one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales; read as a possessive with no apostrophe

explanation.surface: A list of reading matter, as if a corpse had been found among stories by two old authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tales' serves both authors: Richardson's Pamela and Chaucer's Reeve's (Tale).
explanation.definitionFit: In Agatha Christie's novel The Body in the Library, a second murder victim is the girl guide Pamela Reeves.

clue.text: University dons get lost over Brutus?

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the turned word wears another piece inside it
over means the get lost word is turned over, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: scram means get lost, go away

explanation.surface: College lecturers lose their way over a Roman assassin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SCRAM into MARCS; 'dons' (puts on) takes U inside. 'dons' looks like lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Junius Brutus led Caesar's assassins; the question mark marks him as one example of the name.

clue.text: Fairford's friend Latimer, owner of Pemberley we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: Mr Darcy of Pride and Prejudice owns the estate of Pemberley

explanation.surface: A literary friendship, linked by name to Jane Austen's grand hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Walter Scott's Redgauntlet the young hero Darsie Latimer is friend of Alan Fairford.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's Redgauntlet opens with letters between the friends Alan Fairford and Darsie Latimer.

clue.text: Visibly in awe of Triamond's mother

definitions.meaning: openmouthed with wonder, staring with jaw dropped
in Spenser's Faerie Queene the fay mother of the knight Triamond and his brothers

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions: open-mouthed with wonder, and the fairy mother of Triamond in Book IV of Spenser's Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means gaping in amazement; the other is a character's name in Spenser's epic.

clue.text: No. sixteen broadcast at full length

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: No. is written as NO

explanation.surface: Song number sixteen is played on the radio in its complete version.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means unabridged, in full, without any shortening.

clue.text: Split, a city not fully understood

indicators.note: not fully means only part of the run of words is used, a stretch inside them

explanation.surface: Split, the Croatian port, is a city that remains partly a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'sPLIT A CITy'; Split looks like a verb but is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied and understood without being said.

clue.text: Recalling Avon as a child, at first he loved it!

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so everything from Avon to the child's first letter is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written; that the run also reads backwards inside these words is a coincidence of the build, since at first takes the C

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word child is taken

explanation.surface: Thinking back on the Avon of one's childhood, a man remembers his early love for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer does run backwards through 'Avon as a c', but the setter's 'at first' takes just the C of child, so it is that pick, not a bare hidden run. The definition jokes that the great lover loved 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is a byword for a lifelong lover and womaniser.

clue.text: Host with note bearing, "The Trespasser's Siegmund"

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a host
one's air is one's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A host whose demeanour is noted, introducing a character from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In D H Lawrence's novel The Trespasser the violinist hero is Siegmund MacNair.

clue.text: Most demanding way to follow a writer

indicators.note: to follow means the way word comes after the writer

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The hardest path to take is the one after an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest means strictest, the most severe in what it asks of people.

clue.text: Holy man cropping up everywhere in Galsworthy's play

parts.note: ST is short for saint
rife means widespread, found everywhere

explanation.surface: A saint keeps appearing all over a Galsworthy drama.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy's 1909 play Strife dramatises an industrial dispute at a tin-plate works.
